narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Jerkin' originated in Los Angeles in 2008, initially as a dance performed by gang members at parties.
It gained widespread popularity in 2009 through the music of the New Boyz and Audio Push, eventually spreading across the US and internationally.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally an 'anti-dance' within gang culture, it transitioned into a competitive performance style showcased at events and on YouTube.
It is a social dance often performed in crews.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is defined by detailed footwork.
Key moves include the 'jerk' (moving legs in and out), the 'reject' (backward leg rotation), the 'dip' (steps followed by a block), and the 'pindrop' (rapid leg rotation below the knee).
Watch for Jerk, Reject, Dip.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (-bhPauFonp0)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Performed in crews or solo in street settings.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music, known as 'jerk rap', is characterized by upbeat, dance-oriented hip-hop.
In the 2020s, the sound evolved to include faster tempos, melodic synth layers, and abstract, off-kilter lyrics.
Listen for the Synthesizers, Drum machines.
Upbeat hip-hop tracks with dance-oriented rhythms; 2020s revival tracks feature faster tempos and melodic synth layers.

scenes.title: The people
narration: New Boyz, Audio Push, The Ranger$, Rej3ctz, Xaviersobased, and the 1c34 collective.
The dance spread from the US West Coast to the East Coast, France, Germany, and Latin American countries like the Dominican Republic and Panama.
A subgenre of hip-hop and street dance, with later influences from cloud rap, plugg music, and digicore.

steps_as_taught.name: Advanced Reject
steps_as_taught.description: A normal reject where you twist your foot inwards on your toes.

steps_as_taught.name: Melbourne Shuffle
steps_as_taught.description: Pick your non-dominant foot, make a twist on your heel, then toe, heel, toe.

steps_as_taught.name: Heel-Toe
steps_as_taught.description: Carve the heel by twisting in and out with one foot while swinging the other foot up and down.

steps_as_taught.name: Heel-Toe Step
steps_as_taught.description: Carve with your heel again, then carve with your toe right after, followed by a step.

steps_as_taught.name: Criss-Cross
steps_as_taught.description: Keep feet separated, put them together, then separate them and cross the opposite way.

steps_as_taught.name: Steez Step
steps_as_taught.description: Turn to one side, then jump to the other side.
